A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MMDocIR benchmark, retrieval tasks, datasets, and models. The complete text, equations, tables, figures, and v2 appendices A–H support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original page- and layout-retrieval experiments in Tables 5–6 and annotation-consistency measurements in Table 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original retrieval experiments and adds efficiency measurements in Table 9 and a detailed ViDoRe query audit in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The DPR-Phi3 and Col-Phi3 encoders, similarity functions, contrastive objectives, and ColPali-based hard-negative selection remain unchanged. v1 Section 5 moves to v2 Appendix C; the additional training implementation disclosures do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both retain the evaluation corpus of 313 documents across ten domains and 1,658 questions, plus seven training datasets containing 6,878 documents and 73,843 questions. The expanded ViDoRe audit concerns an already examined benchmark; its revised sample count does not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GTE to the layout-retrieval comparisons using OCR-text and VLM-text at Recall@1, @5, and @10. GTE already participated in page retrieval in v1, but was absent from v1's layout-results table. The other retrieval comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an efficiency evaluation measuring storage, indexing time, and search time on an A100 40GB GPU, with image/text batch sizes of 4/256. The ViDoRe audit's stated sample changes from 1,180 to 2,400 questions, with explicit subset-selection rules. VLM-text construction also now lists QwenVL2.5 alongside GPT-4o, without establishing which existing results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a quantitative efficiency study, page-text length and truncation analysis, and a structured ViDoRe suitability audit with category definitions and subset counts. Existing OCR/VLM and image/hybrid comparisons are retained and reorganized into summary tables.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 400-question annotation-agreement comparison and its precision, recall, and F1 reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All page-retrieval scores are retained. v2 adds GTE layout scores, efficiency measurements, and the finding that 222 of 2,400 audited ViDoRe questions are suitable. Five existing hybrid-layout result rows change; for example, DPR-Phi3's macro Recall@10 changes from 59.9 in v1 Table 6 to 55.5 in v2 Table 11.

T1.justification: The dual-task mathematical definition and Equations 1–6 are retained, with the model equations relocated to Appendix C. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The dual-task benchmark contribution and headline findings remain unchanged. v2 corrects the conclusion's training-question count from 173,843 to 73,843, matching the existing dataset table, although the abstract retains the inconsistent larger count.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving text truncation and the absence of native-text training for visual retrievers, and develops accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. It explicitly identifies failures of layout-label construction for complex or cross-modal evidence. It also changes the interpretation of token-level layout retrieval from no advantage in v1 Section 6.4 to a marginal advantage in v2 Section 5.4.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents training batch size, epoch count, image resizing, shared weights, hard-negative count, GPU hardware, and LoRA/FlashAttention/DeepSpeed usage. Tables 12–13 provide construction tools and exact baseline checkpoints. Dataset access instructions and annotation licensing conditions are also expanded. These disclosures substantially extend the information available for reproducing existing experiments.

R1.justification: v1's brief ViDoRe criticism becomes a detailed positioning argument in Appendix F, covering query suitability, ambiguous single-answer labels, document incompleteness, and exclusion from retrieval experiments. v2 also adds a DocVQA benchmark overview and references for training infrastructure and preprocessing tools.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Dataset-construction details move to Appendix B, model training to Appendix C, and retriever descriptions to Appendix D. Experimental discussion is divided into additional sections, with a limitations section and an appendix contents guide.

P2.justification: Main result tables are condensed while full comparisons appear in Appendix A. Figure 3 is expanded, Figure 4 redisplays dataset modality statistics, and Figures 5–14 add document, layout, and annotation illustrations. New comparison summaries, efficiency, resource, checkpoint, and audit tables accompany substantial template and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially reduces v1's reproducibility gaps through training configurations and exact baseline checkpoints, replaces qualitative cost remarks with measured efficiency comparisons, and supports its benchmark positioning with a documented ViDoRe audit. These materially strengthen the paper's evidence and practical usefulness. Dataset-count inconsistencies and misleading table captions remain, but the gains outweigh these limitations.
